description: Reviewed target-fit exclusions for the UK terminal battery (schema 2 per #610). Each entry defers one calibration target whose |relative error| breaches the 25% release bound, with the defect diagnosed, tracked, and owned elsewhere; the receipt records the reasoning, approver, adjudication reference, approval date, and expiry. The gate keeps the target BOUND in calibration (exclusion applies to the release fence only, never the solve), reports dormant entries, FAILS stale ones (targets back inside the bound), and FAILS expired ones until the adjudication is renewed, so this register cannot rot.

hmrc/state_pension_income_band_50_000_to.reason: Calibration-competition residual, not a data defect: the SPI state-pension amount band for total income GBP 50,000 to 70,000 (2023-24 Table 3.7, uprated by the new State Pension rate the engine pays) fitted at +23.4% on v21 and +27.6% on v21b (target GBP 5.26bn); the state-pension family sums 6.9% over its target because the engine pays every recipient the 2025-26 rate while the taxpayer counts by band fit within 1%, and this band carries the residual after the reserved income band donors moved the surrounding bands. Deferred four weeks while the state-pension amount anchor is scoped (PolicyEngine/chronicle#280 lane).
hmrc/state_pension_income_band_50_000_to.adjudication: PolicyEngine/microcosm#1006 (issue comment 5812206367, the register rulings María gave in session: ruling D6 of 2026-09-23; income-anchor lane, PolicyEngine/chronicle#280)
